name: Ironhand Workshop Augmentation Interface Gauntlets
description:
Open-palm gauntlets designed to interface directly with cybernetic hand augmentations. The gauntlets' interior is lined with contact points that seat against standard augmentation port locations, providing power regulation, diagnostic feedback, and signal amplification for augmented hands. The exterior is utilitarian matte-gray polymer.

Essential for augmented individuals whose cybernetic hands require periodic calibration or whose augmentation models draw more power than their internal batteries can sustain during heavy use.
functionality: Augmentation power regulation, diagnostic interface, signal amplification
what_it_says: Your hands aren't original equipment and they need external support to run at full capacity.
story_hooks: An Augmentation Interface Gauntlet is found running at maximum power output with no hand inside it — something is drawing power through the contact points from the other side.

physical_description.visual_profile: Industrial-grade forearm gauntlets that extend from mid-palm to mid-bicep, designed with purpose-built ergonomics. The open-palm construction leaves fingers and palm exposed while the reinforced wrist and forearm sections provide structural support. Appearance is deliberately utilitarian—no aesthetic flourishes, pure function.
physical_description.fit: Compression-fit with anatomical shaping to accommodate standard augmentation port locations. Snug around the wrist and forearm to maintain contact point pressure, while the open palm allows full dexterity and natural hand positioning during work or calibration procedures.
physical_description.primary_material: Matte-gray industrial polymer composite with conductive threading woven into interior contact zones. Exterior shows signs of reinforced stress distribution panels at wrist joints.
physical_description.texture: Smooth, hard polymer exterior with subtle ribbed reinforcement ridges running along forearm sections. Interior is textured with micro-contact pads and barely-visible conductive trace pathways for augmentation interfacing.
physical_description.color_scheme: Matte industrial gray with charcoal accent stitching along seams. Interior contact zones have faint copper-oxide patina from repeated augmentation port contact. No logos or branding visible.
physical_description.closures: Friction-fit magnetic closure system at the wrist with secondary velcro load-bearing strap across the forearm. No zipper—designed for quick removal and installation during augmentation maintenance.
distinctive_features: Interior contact point grid calibrated to standard augmentation port configurations
Embedded micro-diagnostics display (barely visible LED strip along outer wrist)
Power regulation circuit traces visible as faint metallic lines on inner surface
Asymmetrical palm opening—left gauntlet mirrors right for orientation flexibility
Cooling vents along knuckle area to dissipate power regulation heat
Reinforced thumb and index finger guides for grip stability during calibration work
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 functional—working-class augmentation maintenance gear. Not cheap corpo-luxury, but quality industrial equipment indicating someone who maintains serious chrome.
physical_description.cultural_context: Signals augmented labor—fixer, mechanic, industrial worker, or augmentation technician. Wearing these openly indicates prosthetic dependency and mechanical augmentation status. Common in maintenance zones, workshops, and medical compliance environments.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained but clearly used. Interior shows contact wear from repeated augmentation docking. Exterior may have scuffs and minor polymer stress marks from heavy industrial work.
